findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source of the current compilation, including diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None). Previously, diagnostics like MsgPack004/MsgPack003 etc. that were created with a null/None location (e.g. via GetIdentifierLocation returning null) would be reported; now they silently vanish. It also drops diagnostics located in a syntax tree from another compilation. This is a global filter on all analyzer diagnostics, beyond the narrow crash fix, and could suppress diagnostics users currently see.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009/012/018 verifiers) at base and head; add a case where the diagnostic is created with a null location from a partial or source-declared type and assert it is still reported. Any test whose expected diagnostic disappears fails.

findings.claim: The wrapper is applied only to reportDiagnostic, while the crash fix covers just two of the three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites. Line 735 (the reporter's first site) is not changed in this diff. If it is still reachable for a metadata closed generic struct, the IndexOutOfRangeException persists.
